thread:
alex: FYI — customer (Acme) opened an escalation: their Go app saw long hangs and double billing on some requests. They say Go SDK v0.9.3 is retrying despite context cancel. Logs attached. tagging @maria @sahil

maria: Can you paste a tiny repro or the log snippet? first thing to check: are they using context with deadline and/or setting http.Client timeout? Go http transport + retries are a common foot-gun.

alex: Log excerpt:
```
2024-05-07T14:12:10Z request_id=rid_abc123 status=500 msg="server error, retrying"
2024-05-07T14:12:40Z request_id=rid_abc123 status=200 latency=28.7s msg="finished"
2024-05-07T14:12:40Z user_ctx=user-42 err="context canceled"
```
Customer code (simplified):
```go
c := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY")) // v0.9.3 default opts
ctx := context.Background()
req := c.NewCompletionRequest("gpt-open", "hello")
resp, err := c.Do(req.WithContext(ctx))
// they cancel somewhere else after a timer but still see long server-side work and retried requests
```
They also said they use background contexts and rely on SDK internal retries.

sahil: Two quick things likely happening: 1) No per-request deadline/timeout on the context -> goroutine waits on network read; 2) SDK retry loop may retry on 5xx and spawn new HTTP requests without re-checking ctx deadline early enough. Both mean extra tokens billed when upstream eventually completes.

maria: Immediate mitigation options for the customer: set a hard timeout on the HTTP transport or pass a context with deadline, and reduce SDK retries. Example config:
```go
httpClient := &http.Client{
  Timeout: 20 * time.Second,
  Transport: &http.Transport{
    MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 8,
    IdleConnTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
  },
}
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey,
  redwood.WithHTTPClient(httpClient),
  redwood.WithMaxRetries(1), // reduce duplicate attempts
)
// and always do:
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 15*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req = req.WithContext(ctx)
```
Also ensure you always call resp.Body.Close() to avoid leaked connections.

alex: I asked the customer to try that. They replied that they can't easily change their global http client because other parts of their app rely on longer timeouts. Any other approach?

sahil: If they can't change global timeouts, let them supply a per-request context with deadline (recommended). SDK should respect that. If the SDK version is misbehaving, we can also ask them to set header `X-Redwood-Disable-Retries: 1` as a temporary workaround (we'll support this header in the server) or set SDK option to disable retries. Also trace the request ids in our logs to confirm duplicate billing.

maria: I inspected the SDK code in v0.9.3 — there is a retry loop that builds a new http.Request each attempt, but it wasn't re-wrapping the request with the caller ctx until after the first attempt. That makes the first retry not see the canceled context. Quick fix: ensure we call req = req.WithContext(ctx) inside every retry iteration before client.Do(req). I'll open a PR.

alex: Customer wants refund for doubled tokens for the impacted window (~120 requests). Can support issue credits?

sahil: Yes, let's issue credits for confirmed duplicate-charge windows. I'll file a billing ticket and tag @finance. Also mark this as P2 and block customer-facing SDK v0.9.x auto-upgrades.

maria: Created GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/842 and draft PR with test that simulates canceled context and verifies no extra retries after cancel. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/999 (WIP). Patch proposal in comment: ensure WithContext is applied before retries, and check ctx.Err() inside retry backoff before new attempt.

sahil: Temporary server-side mitigation: we can make the server honor an inbound `x-redwood-request-id` and dedupe retries from same client within short window. Also enable debug logging for the customer: `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` and ask them to send us the `x-redwood-trace` header values so we can match server logs.

alex: Thanks — I'll apply the workaround (disable retries + per-request ctx) for the customer, request trace headers, and escalate billing credits. I'll follow up after PR merges. :thumbsup:

maria: After PR merges we should cut a patch release v0.9.4 and notify customers in release notes about best practices: always pass context with deadline, set http.Client.Timeout for long-running flows, and prefer disabling SDK retries if you implement your own idempotency.

support-bot: Created ticket S-2024-7423 for billing refund, assigned to finance.

alex: Closing loop with customer now. Will paste final resolution here when done.
